page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine in the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system provides 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside a bundled 120 GB NVMe solid-state drive and 1 public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture includes x86_64 vector and cryptographic extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and VAES.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution efficiency paired with throughput constraints typical of a dual-thread allocation. Single-core execution in stress-ng reached 3,610.59, and data compression routines demonstrated top-tier throughput with 39.56 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 17.62 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, parallel workloads are restricted by the low core count, resulting in lower-tier results across multi-core Geekbench (2,259.0) and PassMark CPU tests (4,914.73). Large-block memory throughput remains moderate at 45.94 GB/sec read and 40.59 GB/sec write.

Because of the dedicated AMD EPYC core slice and included local NVMe SSD, the instance delivers predictable single-core performance without multi-tenant CPU contention. It is technically suitable for lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch processing, internal microservices, and modest testing environments, whereas parallel computational tasks and enterprise databases require configurations with higher core density.
description: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is a general-purpose instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute lineup, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single dual-threaded AMD EPYC physical core clocked at 2.0 GHz. The node includes 8.0 GB of system memory, 120 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and standard instruction extensions including AVX-512 and VAES. Benchmark profiles show strong single-threaded throughput, marked by upper-tier compression speeds, alongside average memory bandwidth of 45.94 GB/sec read and 40.59 GB/sec write. Multi-threaded capacity is limited by the two-vCPU ceiling, as reflected in lower multi-core Geekbench and PassMark scores. With dedicated CPU allocation and bundled high-speed NVMe storage, this instance is suited for lightweight web application serving, compression pipelines, microservices, and development environments requiring consistent single-thread execution.
